## 2026-11-05T11:14:02Z - DIRECTOR: R3 cadence design cross-review and bounded revision
- Bot relation: BOT_RULES; runtime configuration not checked. Git/work log checked at this timestamp, HEAD `82b5f216e`. Resumes the 09:40 task card after the owner-directed handoff audit. Same queue item 2; no new priority or research work.
- SHOWN independent review: Bohr returned INCOMPLETE for implementation approval. Three blockers: the existing Slack worker accepts only 1,024 input bytes/single finding; descendant ownership after supervisor death is unspecified; monitoring-health transport and already-pending delivery under source/cursor limits are unspecified. Source comparison confirms the 4 MiB queue-copy, 4,096-row/per-query 1 MiB projection, 16,384-event and 16 MiB image limits. No existing component is claimed to implement this revision.
- Decision proposed: retain one foreground watcher service, not a new job/timer. Replace the proposed nested summary worker with synchronous bounded HTTPS in the isolated cycle child. Terminal alerts retain the independently reviewed eight-second worker and existing single-finding contract unchanged. This is a design amendment, not a change to installed or accepted source.

### R3 revised contract A: bounded summary and transport
- A normal summary has exactly `schema`, `release`, `observed_ms`, `findings`, `health`. Schema is the fixed integer 1; release obeys the existing 8-40 lowercase-alphanumeric rule; observation time obeys the existing epoch bound. Findings is a canonical sorted list of at most 93 unique objects, exactly `scope`, `condition`, `first_observed_ms`, from the existing release-specific 90 account/three host roster. Retained pending findings keep their durable original first-observed time, even if no longer active. Unknown/quiet semantics remain unchanged. No arbitrary strings or fields.
- Health is a sorted list of at most five unique objects, exactly `condition`, `observed_ms`, `affected`. Conditions are the fixed roster `cursor_near_capacity`, `source_copy_unavailable`, `queue_evidence_limit`, `cursor_unavailable`, `cursor_capacity`. `affected` is a canonical subset of the nine account scopes; cursor-wide health uses an empty list. Times describe this cycle's detection, not an invented historical onset. These are monitoring faults, not substitute account findings or evidence that a missing source is quiet.
- Encode the complete schema with ASCII JSON; the Slack `text` is the fixed summary title plus that JSON. Enforce BOTH the inner text <= 20,000 ASCII bytes and the final `{"text": ...}` HTTPS body <= 24,576 bytes before POST. No truncation, chunking, alternate channel or fallback to the one-item sender. Oversize/invalid data produces a fixed local terminal fault without clearing any pending state. Actual Slack acceptance/rendering remains an operational test, not inferred from these local limits.
- The summary sender executes directly in the cycle child: one literal `hooks.slack.com` HTTPS request, existing constrained webhook path, verified TLS, no environment proxy, redirects, SDK background worker or retries. Reuse the corrected exact Content-Length/complete `ok` acknowledgement rules, not a permissive new parser. Socket operations use the smaller of five seconds and remaining cycle time. The supervisor's 40-second cycle deadline contains DNS/connect/read as far as process termination is effective; do not promise an eight-second total summary send. No request/body/token/error text is logged. The token is read by the child from the existing protected credential mount, never sent through argv, environment, stdout or supervisor IPC.
- Remove the proposed summary-worker IPC entirely; the existing 1,024-byte terminal worker stays unchanged. Supervisor-to-child input is a fixed bounded control message (<= 2,048 bytes) naming release, launch generation and health suppression state only; child-to-supervisor output is <= 1,024 ASCII bytes, fixed enumerated outcome plus acknowledged health codes. No finding payload, source rows, balances or credentials cross those control pipes. Read at cap+1; oversized/partial/extra output is a terminal fault. Drain within the cycle deadline; no pipe can block the supervisor indefinitely.

### R3 revised contract B: single-child ownership and restart exclusion
- Linux-only, one single-threaded supervisor. At startup, safely open a separately provisioned, service-owned 0600 `supervisor.lock` regular file (one link, no symlinks) inside the existing protected cursor directory; require its containing ancestry/identity protections. Hold a nonblocking exclusive flock on this stable inode for the supervisor lifetime. Do not create, unlink, replace or reseed the lock at startup/recovery. Cursor-image locking continues to use its independent directory descriptor. Provisioning and host proof remain separately authorized.
- One cycle means one child, no grandchildren. The summary cycle must not call the terminal worker or any subprocess/fork API. Before accessing credentials or sources, child bootstrap creates its own process group, arms Linux parent-death SIGKILL, checks that its parent PID is still the expected supervisor, retains the inherited lifetime-lock open-file description, and waits for a bounded launch gate. Parent records the owned child PID/group and pipe handles, verifies its child/group identity, then releases that gate. A failed or timed-out bootstrap never receives work authority; only an owned unreaped child/group is signalled. No scan-and-kill by name, release prefix or unrelated PID.
- Child inherits the already locked lifetime descriptor without unlocking it; it closes it only at exit. A fresh supervisor may launch work only after it acquires that same protected inode's exclusive lock, so a surviving old child blocks replacement work. Parent-death SIGKILL plus the parent-PID race check addresses a supervisor crash; the lock is a second non-overlap fence, not an orphan killer. Child performs no credential/UID/capability changes that would clear parent-death protection. The bootstrap must test this protocol on Linux before operational acceptance.
- Supervisor uses a monotonic 30-second slot clock. Slot zero starts immediately; no overlap and no catch-up. A skipped slot is disclosed as missed observation time, not replayed. All child bootstrap, source reads/copies, image work, direct POST and output handling share 40 seconds; an additional five-second cleanup reserve bounds intended terminate/reap work. On expiry or SIGTERM, stop scheduling, terminate the owned group, escalate to SIGKILL, then reap the owned direct child before reporting clean termination. If reaping cannot complete, fail visibly without claiming cleanup; the still-held descriptor prevents launching a replacement while that child survives. A SIGTERM received between cycles cannot start another child.
- The existing effective `KillMode=control-group`, stop deadline and restart/start-limit graph must be verified at deployment; the reviewed renderer is not that proof. It remains a separate manager-level boundary for crash cleanup and restart rate. No application auto-retry inside a cycle; only subsequent planned cycles or the already reviewed manager policy may repeat an uncertain external acceptance. An uninterruptible kernel call can defeat an elapsed-time target; do not report a stronger hard real-time guarantee.

### R3 revised contract C: health, capacity and delivery of older evidence
- Keep normal findings, pending notices and retained event digests in the existing protected image. Health delivery does NOT require inserting a digest/finding or successfully writing that image. It uses the same validated recipient and the SAME one-POST-per-cycle summary; a corrupt/unreadable cursor allows health-only transmission, never guessed/reconstructed pending evidence. A summary with persisted pending notices plus health remains one external attempt, not two.
- Read/validate a durable pending snapshot first. Try staging new observations in a transaction. If staging fails at a declared source/image/event limit, roll back all uncommitted new evidence and retain the last validated pending snapshot. Attempt those already-durable pending notices plus the applicable health fault. If accepted, acknowledge ONLY the exact old batch using protected persistence; never mark unread/unstaged source events consumed. If persistence fails, leave delivery unconfirmed/replayable. This explicitly revises the earlier blanket 'no acknowledgement at capacity': new evidence cannot be consumed, but existing pending evidence must not be silently stranded behind it.
- If source copying exceeds 4 MiB, its two-second/512-step copy budget, or source access is unavailable, mark that source's affected observations unknown and emit `source_copy_unavailable`; do not label the limit as data corruption. If the adapter exceeds 4,096 rows, a 1 MiB projected-text budget or query-instruction budget, emit `queue_evidence_limit` and unknown evidence for that account. Continue other valid accounts and existing pending delivery. Distinguish these fixed reasons in bounded producer results; do not infer a particular reason from today's generic `None` return. They are observation-coverage faults, not silent success or authorization to raise limits/delete queue history.
- At >= 12,288 retained digests OR >= 12 MiB encoded image, add `cursor_near_capacity`. If staging would exceed 16,384 digests or 16 MiB encoded image, roll back new staging, add `cursor_capacity`, perform the single old-pending/health attempt and exit nonzero. An invalid/missing/unreadable image adds `cursor_unavailable`, permits only the one health attempt and exits nonzero. The existing watcher OnFailure path may separately report terminal failure; it cannot be the sole reporting mechanism for a full cursor, and it is not owner-receipt proof.
- Nonfatal health uses supervisor-memory suppression, not a second ledger: repeat a still-present acknowledged health code no more than once per 30 monotonic minutes; retry unconfirmed codes only at the next planned cycle, at most one POST per cycle. Known healthy observations rearm it; unknown does not. Fatal cursor faults exit after their one attempt. Restart loses suppression and can repeat; the existing manager's start limit, if verified, bounds restart bursts. This consciously trades durable health exactly-once for not depending on a broken/full cursor. Summary transport failure does not clear normal pending or advance health acknowledgement; local fixed error plus terminal disposition reports the remaining failure. If Slack itself is down, no delivery is claimed.
- Recovery remains manual and separately authorized: stop only this watcher; preserve image plus stable lock inode and receipt, hashes/owner/mode; examine an offline duplicate; demonstrate exact retained digest membership, pending/ack state and source/cutoff under a reviewed larger bounded capacity or evidence-preserving repair; acquire the existing lifetime and image locks before any replacement; then separately authorize restart and prove output. Never unlink the lifetime lock, discard events, advance cutoff, prune rows or reset the seed to resume. No repair/recovery automation is introduced.

### Proof and disposition
- Failure matrix addition to the existing 09:40 cases: 93 pending plus all five health codes at maximum release/time; outer/inner byte caps and exact JSON/IPC schemas; old sender/terminal contract unchanged; no summary descendants; parent death before/after launch gate; lifetime lock inherited through child startup and supervisor restart; child stuck at each phase; attempted overlapping supervisor; lock/image replacement; new staging full while old pending exists; unknown source vs copy/query limits; health-only send with corrupt/full image; one-POST enforcement; suppression/known-clear/restart/uncertain POST; batch acknowledgement persistence failure. Reference trace must account for every old pending notice and every health code, either in a bounded summary or a disclosed terminal fault.
- Sources checked for design semantics, not host proof: Linux man-pages `https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html` (parent-death timing/credential caveats), `https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html` (inherited open-file-description lock lifetime). Slack chat.postMessage documentation was opened but is not an incoming-webhook delivery receipt or authorization to switch transport.
- READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW for the revised design only. No code/test/config/credential/host/schedule/send action. Implementation remains outside this task card's stop boundary until design review closes. What do I know that could change the owner's decision that I have not yet said? Final bounded design-review correction; stop on a further blocker rather than begin implementation or another redesign.
- Fixed identity roster: 21 health keys. The three cursor-wide codes (`cursor_near_capacity`, `cursor_unavailable`, `cursor_capacity`) each have one distinct global key. The two source codes (`source_copy_unavailable`, `queue_evidence_limit`) each have nine per-account keys using the canonical sorted account roster. Define a versioned bit position for every exact `(code, scope)`; globals use an explicit global identity, never an account name. No dynamically supplied scope or bit position. A grouped health JSON entry lists only its affected eligible account keys; its global variant has an empty `affected` list.
- Replace the child result with exactly `schema`, `release`, `generation`, `observed_ms`, `outcome`, `present`, `known_clear`, `unknown`, `acknowledged`. Version 1, exact release and 32-lowercase-hex launch generation, bounded epoch and enumerated outcome; masks are exact integers (not booleans), 0..2^21-1. Present/known-clear/unknown are disjoint and together cover all 21 keys. Acknowledged must be a subset of present, of the keys actually included in that single POST, and of the launch's eligible (not suppressed) keys; it is zero unless the exact complete Slack acknowledgement was accepted. No output finding text, account balances, token, exception or response body. Complete JSON <= 1,024 bytes, no extra fields/trailing payload, no stale generation. Invalid result is a terminal fault, not an implicit all-clear.
- Producer meaning: a source-copy key is known-clear only after a successful bounded copy of the correctly identified account; a queue-limit key is known-clear only after a valid complete bounded adapter read. If the preceding copy is unavailable, the queue-limit key is unknown, not clear or presumed over-limit. Cursor capacity keys are known-clear only after successfully inspecting valid matching state and determining that specific threshold is below its limit; an unreadable cursor makes those capacity keys unknown and `cursor_unavailable` present. Global unavailability is known-clear only on a successful matching image read. Present limits require the corresponding explicit producer result, not guesses from generic failures. Unknown observations never rearm any key.
- Supervisor maintains one volatile monotonic next-eligible time per key. At launch it sends exactly a schema/release/generation plus one 21-bit `suppressed` mask in <= 2,048 bytes (no clock values or secret data). Each acknowledged key gets completion-monotonic-time + 1,800 seconds; each known-clear key resets its deadline; unknown and unacknowledged present leave it unchanged. Expiry allows a continuing condition to notify again; a new affected account uses a different bit and is immediately eligible. Suppression is computed at launch; an expiry during a cycle becomes eligible at the following planned cycle, not an extra POST. Restart can repeat acknowledged health, as disclosed; no second durable ledger.
- The child observes and returns all health states even when sending none; filtering governs transmission only. The parent applies state changes only to a complete matching-generation result. On malformed/missing result it clears neither pending evidence nor suppression and follows terminal failure handling. Fatal cursor health still permits only its one attempt then nonzero exit. Already-durable normal findings never share these suppression bits and preserve the cursor/acknowledgement rules in the prior revision.
- Required deterministic traces: A accepted then newly affected B must be included before A's 30-minute expiry; unknown must preserve A; known-clear must rearm A; queue-copy failure must not clear queue-limit health; corrupt cursor must not clear capacity warnings; acknowledgement must match the exact transmitted eligible keys; out-of-roster/overlapping/incomplete/stale masks must fail; unconfirmed POST acknowledges zero; parent crash retains the disclosed non-durable health limitation.
